newsitem.title: USA: New York may adopt 'wild card' bank charter law.
newsitem.headline: New York may adopt 'wild card' bank charter law.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki has proposed a bill that would automatically grant to banks charted in the state any powers given to nationally chartered banks under federal law.
New York is one of only seven states that do not have a so-called "wild card" provision, the governor said in a memorandum accompanying the bill.
"The bill would help preserve the New York banking charter as an attractive alternative to the federal charter," the memo said.

The bill would authorize the state banking superintendent "to permit state-chartered banks and trust companies to exercise any right, power, privilege or benefit to enagge in any activity and to enter any loan, investment or transaction in which a national bank, acting either directly or through a subsidiary or sudsidiaries, may lawfully engage or into which it may lawfully enter," the memo said.

Last November, U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig, whose office oversees all nationally chartered banks, said he would begin permitting banks to enter a variety of non-banking businesses through subsidiaries.
Court decisions in recent years have also given national banks new powers.
"The pace of these changes may be expected to continue," the governor's memo said.
